config.title: Build virtualized list rendering logic

intro.title: Build virtualized list rendering logic
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a virtualized list rendering logic to efficiently display large datasets in a web application. You will learn how to render only the visible items on the screen, significantly improving performance by reducing the number of DOM elements. The core programming concept involves calculating which items are in the viewport based on scroll position and dynamically updating the displayed content. You will use JavaScript to handle scroll events, manage state for the visible range, and apply CSS for positioning. This exercise introduces you to performance optimization techniques essential for handling large lists in real-world applications.
intro.usecase: Virtualized list rendering is essential for performance in data-heavy applications like social media feeds, e-commerce product catalogs, and analytics dashboards. When you scroll through thousands of posts in Facebook or browse products on Amazon, only the visible items are rendered—dramatically reducing memory usage and improving scroll smoothness. Developers implement this pattern in financial trading platforms displaying real-time stock data, project management tools with large task lists, and messaging apps showing extensive chat histories. Mastering virtualization lets you build responsive interfaces that handle massive datasets without compromising user experience.

objectives: Implement a function to calculate visible items based on scroll position
Construct a virtualized list component that renders only visible items
Initialize and update state variables for scroll position and container dimensions
Apply performance optimizations by limiting DOM nodes to visible items only
Configure event handlers to track scroll position changes
Manipulate CSS properties to position items correctly within the viewport
Integrate measurement calculations to determine item positions and offsets

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React APIs are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and the useState hook from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the VirtualizedList component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named VirtualizedList that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called VirtualizedList that returns null. You can use either function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the VirtualizedList component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a VirtualizedList component function that returns null, ready to hold virtualization logic later.
successCriteria: A component named VirtualizedList is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named VirtualizedList that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function called VirtualizedList that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize state for scroll position
steps.instruction: Inside the VirtualizedList component, use useState to create a state variable named scrollTop initialized to 0.
steps.hint: Call useState(0) and destructure the returned array into scrollTop and a setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for a counter
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a scrollTop state variable initialized to 0, ready to track scroll position.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that declares a scrollTop variable initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an initial value of 0 and naming the variable scrollTop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The scrollTop state isn't properly initialized. Check that you're using useState(0) and destructuring correctly.

steps.title: Define the list data
steps.instruction: Inside the VirtualizedList component, define a constant array named 'items' containing at least 1000 objects, each with an 'id' and 'text' property.
steps.hint: Create a static dataset that the virtualized list will display. Use Array.from() or a loop to generate many items.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a dataset of at least 1000 items that can be used for virtualization.
successCriteria: A constant 'items' array is defined with at least 1000 objects, each having 'id' and 'text' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created an items array, but make sure it has at least 1000 objects with both 'id' and 'text' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The items array is missing or doesn't meet the requirements. Create an array with at least 1000 objects, each with 'id' and 'text'.

steps.title: Create the calculateVisibleRange helper
steps.instruction: Inside the VirtualizedList component, create a helper function named calculateVisibleRange that takes scrollTop as a parameter and returns an object with startIndex and endIndex properties.
steps.hint: The function should calculate startIndex by dividing scrollTop by ITEM_HEIGHT and rounding down. Calculate endIndex by adding the number of items that fit in the viewport (VIEWPORT_HEIGHT / ITEM_HEIGHT) to startIndex, then rounding up.
steps.expectedOutcome: A calculateVisibleRange function is defined inside the component that correctly computes startIndex and endIndex based on scroll position.
successCriteria: The calculateVisibleRange function exists, takes scrollTop as a parameter, and returns an object with startIndex and endIndex properties calculated using ITEM_HEIGHT and VIEWPORT_HEIGHT.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it takes scrollTop as a parameter and returns an object with both startIndex and endIndex properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The calculateVisibleRange function is missing or doesn't match the required structure. It should calculate which items are visible based on scroll position.

steps.title: Create the handleScroll event handler
steps.instruction: Inside your VirtualizedList component, create a function called handleScroll that takes an event parameter and updates the scrollTop state with event.currentTarget.scrollTop.
steps.hint: Define a function that receives the scroll event and calls setScrollTop with the current scroll position from the event.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleScroll function that updates the scrollTop state when called with a scroll event.
successCriteria: A handleScroll function is defined inside the component that calls setScrollTop with event.currentTarget.scrollTop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your handleScroll function takes an event parameter and calls setScrollTop with event.currentTarget.scrollTop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleScroll function isn't quite right. Remember to define it inside the component and update the scrollTop state with the event's scroll position.

steps.title: Add the outer container div with scroll handler
steps.instruction: In the component's return statement, replace the current return value with a div element that has an onScroll handler set to handleScroll and a fixed height from VIEWPORT_HEIGHT.
steps.hint: The div should be scrollable and have a fixed height to create a viewport. Use the onScroll attribute to call your handleScroll function when scrolling occurs.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a scrollable div container with the handleScroll function attached to its scroll event and a fixed height matching VIEWPORT_HEIGHT.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a div element with onScroll={handleScroll} and a style attribute setting height to VIEWPORT_HEIGHT.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your div has both the onScroll handler and a fixed height style.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container div is missing or incomplete. Check that you've added the onScroll handler and set a fixed height.

steps.title: Add the inner container div for positioning
steps.instruction: Inside the outer div you created in the previous step, add an inner div with a height set to the total height of all items (items.length * ITEM_HEIGHT) and position relative.
steps.hint: The inner div should be a child of the outer div. Use style={{ height: totalHeight, position: 'relative' }} where totalHeight is items.length * ITEM_HEIGHT.
steps.expectedOutcome: The inner div will have the correct total height and relative positioning, creating space for the virtualized items to be positioned within.
successCriteria: An inner div is added inside the outer div with style={{ height: items.length * ITEM_HEIGHT, position: 'relative' }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an inner div, but check the height calculation or positioning style.
steps.feedbackWrong: The inner container is missing or incorrect. Make sure to add a div with the proper height and position style inside the outer div.

steps.title: Render only the visible items
steps.instruction: Inside the inner container div, map over the visible range of items to render each item as a div positioned absolutely using its index, ITEM_HEIGHT, and startIndex.
steps.hint: First, call calculateVisibleRange() to get startIndex and endIndex. Then use items.slice(startIndex, endIndex + 1).map() to create div elements for each visible item. Set each div's style to position: 'absolute', top: (index - startIndex) * ITEM_HEIGHT + 'px', and height: ITEM_HEIGHT + 'px'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The inner container will display only the items currently visible in the viewport, each positioned correctly based on the scroll position.
successCriteria: The inner div contains a .map() call over items.slice(startIndex, endIndex + 1) that renders div elements with absolute positioning, correct top values, and ITEM_HEIGHT.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're calling calculateVisibleRange() to get startIndex and endIndex, then using items.slice() with those values. Each div needs position: 'absolute', top based on (index - startIndex) * ITEM_HEIGHT, and height: ITEM_HEIGHT + 'px'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The visible items aren't rendering correctly. Check that you're: 1) calling calculateVisibleRange(), 2) slicing items with startIndex and endIndex + 1, 3) mapping to create divs with position: 'absolute', 4) setting top using (index - startIndex) * ITEM_HEIGHT, and 5) setting height to ITEM_HEIGHT.
